summary: Embedding metadata timestamp drift causing cache-miss storms and rerank latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customers using our reranking endpoint in front of the dedicated embedding cache observed sudden latency spikes (tail p99 > 2s) and elevated 5xx from the rerank path starting 2026-03-10 ~09:00 UTC. Impact: production traffic from ClipStream Media (dedicated pool) experienced timeouts and degraded ranking quality due to a high rate of cache misses and subsequent synchronous recompute.

Impact:
- Elevated p95/p99 for /v1/rerank (p99 from 450ms -> 2.3s for affected traffic).
- Increased token costs due to repeated embedding recomputations.
- Intermittent 503/504 responses for some requests behind the rerank route.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: clipstream-dedicated-3
- Region: us-east-1 (prod)
- Embedding model: embedder-lite-384-v2 pinned by customer
- Cache: sharded KV LRU cache fronting embedding service

Steps to reproduce (observed behavior):
1) Customer sends bursty rerank traffic with mixed TTL metadata headers (client includes embed-metadata:ts header).
2) Cache lookup attempted; cache key composed of (model, namespace, embed-metadata:ts).
3) When client clock skewed or header microseconds varied, cache keys didn't match leading to miss and synchronous recompute against embedder process.
4) Under burst, many concurrent recomputes saturated embedding workers causing queueing and retry/backpressure into rerank path.

Logs / Observations:
- KV-cache logs show surge of cache-miss events + unique key cardinality spiking at 09:03 UTC.
- Embed service CPU/GPU utilization at 95% across a subset of hosts.
- Rerank service traces show increased downstream latency waiting on embed RPCs.
- Customer reported that after a client-side release paused (09:20 UTC), the anomaly subsided.

Initial hypothesis:
- Cache key includes a client-provided timestamp header for debugging; clients sometimes send sub-second varying values resulting in effectively unbounded key variants and causing a cache missstorm.

Requested by customer:
- Immediate mitigation to reduce repeated recompute and restore p99 latency to SLA targets.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:35 - Ava Patel (Support): Customer reported p99 spikes and provided sample request headers. Noted embed-metadata:ts present and varying across otherwise identical requests.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Marcus Chen (SRE): Observed unique-key cardinality increase in kv-cache metrics. Opening hotfix/mitigation: treat embed-metadata:ts as non-keyed metadata for cache lookups for affected namespaces.

2026-03-10 11:15 - ClipStream Ops (customer): Confirmed a client-side SDK version deployed yesterday that started sending microsecond timestamps in embed-metadata header. Rolling back to previous release reduced churn temporarily.
2026-03-11 08:45 - Marcus Chen (SRE): Deployed transient gate in kv-cache that strips sub-second precision from embed-metadata:ts for requests to clipstream namespace. Monitoring for 24h.
2026-03-12 14:30 - Ava Patel (Support): Customer reports p99 back within SLA after gate; will coordinate with customer to remove header or standardize TTL behavior in SDK.

2026-03-12 16:10 - Marcus Chen (SRE): Proposal: change cache key derivation to whitelist stable headers; add telemetry to detect high-cardinality header-derived keys and alert. Tracking INT-4120 for platform-wide change.
investigation_notes: Confirmed high-cardinality keys were the proximate cause via kv-cache histogram and unique_key_count metric (x1000 baseline -> spike).
Trace spans indicate rerank requests spend 80-90% of tail wait time on embed derivation when cache miss rate is elevated.
Customer SDK 1.3.7 introduced embed-metadata:ts with sub-second precision; earlier versions omitted the header.
Hotfix gate implemented to normalize timestamp header to second granularity for clipstream namespace; immediate reduction in unique cache keys observed.
Root cause: cache key derivation included unnormalized client-supplied metadata that should not contribute to key space.
resolution: Mitigation applied: transient normalization gate in kv-cache to strip sub-second precision from embed-metadata:ts for the affected namespace and a short-term whitelist to ignore non-keyable headers. Customer rolled back offending SDK release and confirmed latency improvement. Next steps: implement platform-wide key-derivation hardening (INT-4120) to ignore volatile client headers, add cardinality alerts, and update developer docs/SDK to discourage sending microsecond timestamps. Follow-up: schedule postmortem and add permanent fix PR (github.com/redwood/kv-cache/pull/1284).
